allocation_defect.proof: A SIGINT/SIGTERM received during mkdtemp or receipt save was deferred only through save. Exiting that guard replayed interruption before canonical path/dev+inode/owner assignment, so finalizer correctly refused unowned removal and stranded the exact allocation. A receipt-write exception also exited before identity capture. No app process needed to exist for this reachable failure.
allocation_defect.correction: Resolve canonical parent first; defer signals through mkdtemp, exact regular-directory/current-UID/dev+inode capture, owned-name and in-memory owner setup, then persistence. The owner constructor starts no subprocess. Owner/name/persistence errors leave identity available to the finalizer. Removal rechecks canonical path, directory type, UID and exact identity. No unrelated allocation or global cache is adopted.
allocation_defect.counter_evidence: Failure to attest the newly allocated directory itself intentionally remains cleanup FAIL with the path retained. Guessing ownership to delete is unsafe; this is not converted to PASS. Synthetic deferrer test invokes only the installed handler callback, never signals a real process.
